I have nothing on Telltale in the materials available to me. The client store covers only Toil & Trouble, and the firm store holds general practices with no Telltale entry. So I can't say how Telltale wants expert reports reviewed or when it will discuss settlement, and I won't guess. Another client's preferences are also likely confidential, so please don't copy them over without checking. If you want Telltale's approach, ask the Telltale matter team, and share it only if the firm confirms it's allowed.

Here is what the stores do support for Toil & Trouble (B-2).

**Expert work**
- Before engaging any testifying expert, send General Counsel Franklin Oyelaran each proposed expert's name, credentials, prior testimony and fee quote. Get his clearance before anyone is signed.
- Get quotes before any costly testing. Expert and testing costs are the biggest budget swing items.
- The stores say nothing on how Toil & Trouble wants expert reports reviewed. Ask Mr. Oyelaran, and keep any report to the one-page format the client requires.

**Settlement timing**
- Toil & Trouble prefers mediation before expert work. The lesson on file is to bring opposing counsel along by offering early production of key documents and fixed expert dates, with a trigger if mediation fails. This works especially well if the other side fears delay.
- Settlement authority above the set tier needs formal sign-off from the CFO, or from the board in writing. Verbal indications aren't enough, and we must not signal any offer above the tier before sign-off.
- Flag early if the range may exceed the tier, because approval takes time.
- Copy Delphine Moorcroft in risk management on anything touching exposure or coverage.

**Related reminders**
- Tell the GC at once if the case could lead to pulling the TT-6200, because the client has promised its largest retail partners advance warning.
- Staff no more than two lawyers at any deposition or hearing.

I can draft the first one-page report or the expert-clearance request to Mr. Oyelaran if that helps.
